means: Drawn streak lines trailing a moving object - ink marks added to the picture, not an optical effect happening in a lens.
does: Adds graphic streaks behind or around the moving element, and reads instantly as animation rather than photography. Two things to know. It competes with your background: the lines want to eat the location, and on a busy frame the model tends to trade one for the other. And it is not where this project's motion actually comes from - the apparent violence in the reference short is post compositing in short.py's fx_chain (smear, shake, ramp, whiteout), which is exact, repeatable and free, while this tag is a request the sampler may decline. Do not reach for 'motion blur' to do this job: it was tried in the positive here and hazed the entire frame, blowing out four otherwise-good keyframes, and it now lives permanently in the negative.
reach_for_it: a single sakuga beat where the drawing itself should show speed - one or two per film, not on every action shot
used_in: the leaping mid-air volley in derby.json and derby-ep1.json - the one shot in the film that asks for it, marked sakuga in the .movie source
